rubrics.evidence: The agent.patch only modifies LanguagePack.raw (adding a defaultValue param) and I18N.get (routing through pack.raw instead of lodashGet). It does not touch MessageEntry.ts or the describe/describeMessage surface. In the smell.diff, describeMessage in index.ts still composes the line field-by-field (`entry.key@${entry.lang}`, `hits:${entry.hitCount}`, `writes:${entry.cacheWrites}`, `hot:${entry.hotnessLevel}`, `at:${entry.lastUsedAt}`, `text:${entry.content}`), and MessageEntry exposes no describe/summary behavior of its own. The agent's patch leaves this displaced responsibility unchanged, so the facade still narrates the record's lifecycle with zero contribution from the record type.
rubrics.criterion: The knowledge of how a resolved message's metrics (identity, language, hit count, hotness, cache writes, last-use timestamp, content status) become its human-readable description now executes as behavior of the message-record type, and the facade's describe surface routes through it instead of reading the record's metrics field-by-field. Equivalent owner-side seams (one method or a small set of record behaviors) count; a record that only returns raw fields while the line is still composed elsewhere does not.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch does not move the promotion rule to MessageEntry. LanguagePack.shouldPromote(entry) still computes the verdict from the record's raw metrics (entry.hotnessLevel, entry.hitCount, entry.cacheWrites, entry.lastUsedAt), and MessageEntry still has no promotability method. The only changes are LanguagePack.raw gaining a defaultValue parameter and index.ts using pack.raw() for fallback, so the per-language dataset continues to compute the hot-message verdict itself.
rubrics.criterion: The hot-message verdict (which messages rank as promotable based on their hotness, hit count, cache writes and usage recency) is expressed by the message-record type; the per-language dataset asks the record for that verdict when maintaining its hot window instead of computing the rule itself from the record's raw metrics.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch only modifies LanguagePack.ts (adding a defaultValue param to raw()) and index.ts (switching get() to use pack.raw()). It does not touch IntlFormatter.ts or MessageEntry.ts. IntlFormatter.renderEntry still reads entry.content and entry.lang, compares entry.lastRenderedLang !== entry.lang to detect drift, and calls entry.noteRender() to stamp render state back onto the record — exactly the record-driven rendering logic the rubric says should live on MessageEntry (or be reduced to pure compilation in the formatter). The smell remains unrefactored.
rubrics.criterion: Message rendering is driven by the record type rather than done to it: the decisions that read a record's content and language, compare against its last-rendered language to detect drift, and stamp render state (rendered language, render sequence, render outcome) back onto the record are behavior of the record type, with the ICU message machinery used as a collaborator. A formatter left with only pure message compilation (no bulk reads of the record) also satisfies this.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch does not touch IntlFormatter.packNumber; it still pulls the dataset's market fields field-by-field (pack.currency, pack.compact, pack.grouping, pack.minimumFractionDigits, pack.maximumFractionDigits, and pack.lang) to assemble NumberFormat options. LanguagePack only gained a defaultValue on raw(), and formatCurrency still delegates to __formatter__.packNumber(this.__activePack__(), ...), so the per-language dataset does not supply its money/number conventions as a self-described object and the currency path still digs into the dataset's fields.
rubrics.criterion: The money/number conventions of a language (currency code, grouping, digit bounds, and the locale derived for the dataset) are supplied by the per-language dataset type about itself, and the currency path consumes what the dataset provides; the rendering code no longer pulls a dataset's convention and locale fields field-by-field to assemble its options.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch only modifies LanguagePack.ts (adding a defaultValue param to raw()) and index.ts (switching get() to use pack.raw()). It does not touch TranslationCache.ts or MessageEntry.ts at all. In the smell code, TranslationCache.rememberEntry still computes identity as `${entry.lang}#${entry.key}`, decides hot-slot marking via `entry.hotnessLevel >= 2`, decides first constructive write via `entry.cacheWrites === 0 && entry.lastUsedAt > 0`, and bumps the write counter directly with `entry.cacheWrites += 1`. evictEntry likewise re-derives identity and checks raw fields (hitCount, hotnessLevel, cacheWrites, lastUsedAt). Since the patch leaves all of this unchanged, the cache continues to re-derive admission decisions from raw record fields instead of asking the MessageEntry to supply its own cache identity, hot-slot marking, first-write status, and write-count bumping behavior.
rubrics.criterion: The cache's admission decisions about one message derive from identity and status the message-record type provides about itself: a single record-side seam supplies the cache identity used for slot keys, the record's own hotness decides hot-slot marking, the record's own first-write status decides the record's first constructive write (including the miss-counter reset), and the record's cache-write count is bumped through record behavior. The cache no longer re-derives any of these from raw record fields.

rubrics.evidence: The agent.patch only modifies LanguagePack.raw (adding defaultValue) and index.ts get() to use pack.raw() instead of lodashGet; it does not touch TranslationCache.ts or MessageEntry.ts. rubrics.criterion: The prune (eviction) rule for one message is decided by the message-record type: the record exposes the prunability verdict (protected by sufficient hits or hotness, condemned when it was used but never admitted to cache), and the cache's eviction step consumes that verdict while consulting only its own slot ownership.

rubrics.evidence: The smell shows IntlAudit.recordEntryUsage composing the usage line itself by reading entry.key, entry.lang, entry.hitCount, entry.hotnessLevel, entry.cacheWrites, entry.lastUsedAt, and entry.renderCount. rubrics.evidence: The patch removes `lodashGet` from `src/index.ts` and rewrites `I18N.get` to ask the data owner instead of digging: `this.__activePack__().raw(str)` and fallback `this.__packFor__(this.__defaultKey__ || 'zh-CN').raw(str, str)`.
